import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling

/-!
# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam

The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.

The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.

This is not an unconditional Picard representability result: the final declaration below retains
both geometric inputs.  Moreover, at the larger admissible coverage parameter the raw Abel map has
positive-dimensional linear-system fibres in positive genus, so the larger divisor representer
cannot simply be substituted as an open chart source.  The remaining datum-tail construction is
the corrected Altman--Kleiman step: represent the quotient by equality of the induced Picard class,
thereby removing those fibres before applying the Picard representability seam.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
  genus-parameter divisor representer.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible` is the no-argument widened Abel map at the
  unconditional admissible coverage parameter; its legal chart index is chosen internally.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffAdmissible` is the corresponding universal family.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
  source opens.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` is the conditional final assembly
  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)

/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
  exact h.symm

/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the unconditional representer at the
admissible coverage parameter. -/
def universalDivFamAffAdmissible :
    divFamZarAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :=
  (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)

/-- Pullback of the admissible universal family agrees with classification by the unconditional
admissible representer. -/
theorem universalDivFamAffAdmissible_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :
    divFamZarAff.map C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) q
        (universalDivFamAffAdmissible C)
      = (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
  have h := (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    (𝟙 (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C))
  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
  exact h.symm

/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra in
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver in
/-- The widened Abel map at the unconditional admissible coverage parameter.  A legal chart
index whose locus is universal is chosen internally; this declaration does not assert that the
raw Abel map is an open immersion or an atlas. -/
def abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible :
    yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 := by
  classical
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
  let hchart := exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ
    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C)
  let m : ℕ := Classical.choose hchart
  let hZ := Classical.choose_spec hchart
  let Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor := Classical.choose hZ
  have hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
        - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) := by
    change Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
        - (admissibleCoverageParameter
        - (admissibleCoverageParameter
            (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) : ℤ)
    exact (Classical.choose_spec hZ).1
  exact abelSigmaChartAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) m Z hdeg

/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i

/-- The structure morphism read from the admissible Abel map is the structure morphism of the
unconditional admissible divisor representer. -/
lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) i
      = (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom := by
  dsimp only [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible]
  exact chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff
    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) _ _ _ i

/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
unconditional divisor representer. -/
def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
  have hrestrict := chartHom_restrictChart (C := C)
    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i
  have hgenus := chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i
  simpa only [chartHom, affineGenusChart] using
    hrestrict.trans (congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·) hgenus)

/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.

The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
Zariski local representability. -/
def pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts {ι : Type u}
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by

/-!
# Representability of the widened divisor functor

The universal widened class on every divisor chart satisfies the classifier clause, hence
represents the positive-genus divisor functor by `DivScheme`.  The window bound follows from
nonzero genus.  In genus zero the widened functor is terminal, so choosing finite bases internally
gives an unconditional representer without adding a hypothesis to the curve data.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option quotPrecheck false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
set_option maxRecDepth 16000

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Grassmannian Scheme

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

section Curve

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] [IsDominant pi]

noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepChartClassUnivAffRepresentable :
    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))
variable (g : Nat)
variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
  (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))

section Based

variable (r1 r2 : Nat)
variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
  ↥(divisorSections k
    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))

local notation "DivOver" =>
  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)

include hO hchi in
/-- For nonzero genus, the universal widened chart classes represent the divisor functor by
the existing divisor scheme. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_of_ne_zero (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver := by
  let hb := windowBound_pos_of_genus_ne_zero pi hpi g hg hO hchi
  exact divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarAffUniv C hpi g r1 r2 b1
      (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j hO hchi hb)
    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.isDivRepClassifyAff_divFamZarAffUniv
      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 hO hchi i j hb)

omit hchi in
include hO in
/-- At independent curve parameter `gamma ≤ g`, the universal widened chart classes
represent the degree-`g` divisor functor by the existing divisor scheme. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_at
    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
  divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause_at
    (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
    (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (hOAt := hO) (gamma := gamma)
    (hgamma := hgamma) (hchiGamma := hchiGamma)
    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarAffUniv_at C hpi g r1 r2 b1
      (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j hgamma hchiGamma)
    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.isDivRepClassifyAff_divFamZarAffUniv_at
      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hgamma hchiGamma)

end Based

omit hchi in
include hO in
/-- The degree-`g` widened divisor functor has a chosen representer when the curve Euler
parameter is any `gamma ≤ g`. The degree-zero branch remains the terminal object. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAffRepresenter_at
    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy D := by
  classical
  clear hchi
  by_cases hg : g = 0
  · subst g
    exact ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      divFunctorAffZeroRepresentableBy (C := C) (pi := pi)⟩
  · let r1 := Module.finrank k
      ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
    let r2 := Module.finrank k ↥(divisorSections k
      ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
    let b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
        ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
      Module.finBasis k _
    let b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k ↥(divisorSections k
        ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
      Module.finBasis k _
    exact ⟨divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm),
      divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_at
        (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2)
        (gamma := gamma) (hgamma := hgamma) (hchiGamma := hchiGamma)⟩

include hO hchi in
/-- The diagonal widened divisor representer, specialized from the arbitrary-degree producer. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAffRepresenter :
    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy D :=
  divFunctorAffRepresenter_at (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
    (hO := hO) (gamma := g) (Nat.le_refl g) hchi

/-- A chosen scheme representing the widened divisor functor. -/
noncomputable def divRepAffScheme : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).1

omit hchi in
/-- A chosen scheme representing the degree-`g` widened divisor functor at independent
curve parameter `gamma ≤ g`. -/
noncomputable def divRepAffScheme_at {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  (divFunctorAffRepresenter_at (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
    (hO := hO) (gamma := gamma) (hgamma := hgamma) (hchiGamma := hchiGamma)).1

/-- The widened divisor functor is represented by its chosen scheme, with no genus or chart-basis
hypothesis. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy :
    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy (divRepAffScheme C hpi g hO hchi) :=
  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).2

omit hchi in
/-- The degree-`g` widened divisor functor is represented at every independent curve
parameter `gamma ≤ g`. -/
noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_at
    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy
      (divRepAffScheme_at (C := C) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
        (hO := hO) (gamma := gamma) (hgamma := hgamma) (hchiGamma := hchiGamma)) :=
  (divFunctorAffRepresenter_at (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
    (hO := hO) (gamma := gamma) (hgamma := hgamma) (hchiGamma := hchiGamma)).2

end Curve

end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	# The locally certified divisor functor on all test objects: the vehicle (DD-2 stage S6a)
    11	
    12	The Addendum-2 divisor-functor value on an affine test is `DivFamZar C R π n`
    13	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZar`), with base change `DivFamZar.mapAlg`
    14	along arbitrary test changes (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg`).
    15	This file extends it to **all** of `Over (Spec k)` by the bespoke affine-opens limit,
    16	mirroring the globally certified vehicle `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyVehicle`
    17	clause for clause:
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.mapAlgHom`: base change of locally certified divisor
    20	  classes along an **explicit** `k`-algebra map — `DivFamZar.mapAlg` at the induced
    21	  algebra tower, with the functor laws `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id`/`DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp`
    22	  from the S5b laws `DivFamZar.mapAlg_id`/`DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp`.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg`: **the face-change bridge** — along
    24	  an algebra map agreeing with a scalar-tower structure map, the explicit face is the
    25	  instance face (`DivFamZar.mapAlg_congr`, algebra structures with equal structure maps
    26	  are equal).  This is how the S6 general-test statements consume the S5b keystones
    27	  `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq`/`DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`, which are spelled in
    28	  the instance face.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.congr`: transport along an isomorphism of test algebras.
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZar C π n T`: **the vehicle** — compatible families of
    31	  locally certified divisor classes over the affine opens of `T.left`, with
    32	  `divFamZar.eval` the evaluation at an affine open.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n R`: **the affine comparison** — on an
    34	  affine test `overSpec k R` the vehicle collapses by evaluation at the top affine open
    35	  to `DivFamZar C R π n` (the `divFamAffineEquiv` template, clause for clause).
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFam.toZarVehicle`: **the comparison from the globally certified
    37	  vehicle** — componentwise `DivFam.toZar`, compatible by `DivFam.toZar_mapAlg`
    38	  (packaged on the explicit face as `DivFam.toZar_mapAlgHom`); it intertwines the two
    39	  affine comparisons (`divFamZarAffineEquiv_toZarVehicle`).
    40	
    41	Functoriality in `T` along an *arbitrary* morphism of test objects (glued values over
    42	basic-open refinements, the `picEtMap` pattern) is
    43	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMap`; the sheaf statements at arbitrary tests
    44	are `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf`.
    45	
    46	The `k`-algebra structure on section rings is `Over.sectionsAlgebra` and the algebra
    47	structures on the relative curve's section rings are `Scheme.overModule`/
    48	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate
    49	the same instances.
    50	-/

    74	/-! ## Base change of locally certified classes along an explicit algebra map
    75	
    76	`DivFamZar.mapAlg` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg`) is parameterized
    77	by an algebra-tower instance pack `[Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']`.  The vehicle
    78	indexes its compatibilities by the section-restriction maps `Over.resAlgHom`, so it
    79	consumes the explicit-map face — the `DivFam.mapAlgHom` packaging of
    80	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyVehicle`, verbatim. -/

    83	
    84	variable {A A' A'' : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing A'] [Algebra k A']
    85	  [CommRing A''] [Algebra k A'']

    87	/-- Base change of locally certified divisor classes along an explicit `k`-algebra map
    88	of affine tests: `DivFamZar.mapAlg` at the algebra structure `RingHom.toAlgebra` of the
    89	map.  The instance-parameterized `DivFamZar.mapAlg` remains the preferred form whenever
    90	a scalar tower is already in scope. -/
    91	def mapAlgHom (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') : DivFamZar C A π n → DivFamZar C A' π n :=
    92	  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    93	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
    94	  DivFamZar.mapAlg A' n
    95	
    96	/-- `mapAlgHom` along the identity is the identity (`DivFamZar.mapAlg_id`). -/
    97	theorem mapAlgHom_id (F : DivFamZar C A π n) : mapAlgHom (AlgHom.id k A) F = F :=
    98	  DivFamZar.mapAlg_id n F
    99	
   100	/-- `mapAlgHom` along a composite is the composite of the base changes
   101	(`DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp`). -/
   102	theorem mapAlgHom_comp (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : A' →ₐ[k] A'') (F : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   103	    mapAlgHom (ψ.comp φ) F = mapAlgHom ψ (mapAlgHom φ F) :=
   104	  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   105	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (φ.commutes x).symm
   106	  letI : Algebra A' A'' := ψ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   107	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A' A'' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (ψ.commutes x).symm
   108	  letI : Algebra A A'' := (ψ.comp φ).toRingHom.toAlgebra
   109	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A'' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => ((ψ.comp φ).commutes x).symm
   110	  haveI : IsScalarTower A A' A'' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
   111	  (DivFamZar.mapAlg_comp A' n A'' F).symm

   114	
   115	/-- `DivFamZar.mapAlg` depends on the `A`-algebra structure of the target only through
   116	the structure itself: equal algebra structures give equal base changes (the scalar-tower
   117	witnesses are proof-irrelevant).  The congruence backing the face-change bridge
   118	`mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg`. -/
   119	theorem mapAlg_congr {a₁ a₂ : Algebra A A'} (h : a₁ = a₂)
   120	    (t₁ : @IsScalarTower k A A' Algebra.toSMul a₁.toSMul Algebra.toSMul)
   121	    (t₂ : @IsScalarTower k A A' Algebra.toSMul a₂.toSMul Algebra.toSMul)
   122	    (F : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   123	    @DivFamZar.mapAlg k _ C A _ _ π _ A' _ _ a₁ t₁ n F
   124	      = @DivFamZar.mapAlg k _ C A _ _ π _ A' _ _ a₂ t₂ n F := by
   125	  subst h
   126	  rfl

   128	/-- **The face-change bridge**: `mapAlgHom` along an algebra map that agrees with the
   129	structure map of a scalar tower in scope is the instance-based `DivFamZar.mapAlg` of the
   130	tower.  This is how the vehicle statements (spelled at `Over.resAlgHom`) consume the S5b
   131	Zariski keystones (spelled at localization instance packs). -/
   132	theorem mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg [Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower k A A'] (φ : A →ₐ[k] A')
   133	    (hφ : ∀ a, φ a = algebraMap A A' a) (F : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   134	    mapAlgHom φ F = DivFamZar.mapAlg A' n F := by
   135	  unfold mapAlgHom
   136	  exact mapAlg_congr (Algebra.algebra_ext _ _ hφ) _ _ F

   140	/-- Transport of locally certified divisor classes along an isomorphism of test
   141	algebras. -/
   142	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') : DivFamZar C A π n ≃ DivFamZar C A' π n where
   143	  toFun := mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom
   144	  invFun := mapAlgHom e.symm.toAlgHom
   145	  left_inv F := by
   146	    rw [← mapAlgHom_comp, show e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k A from
   147	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a, mapAlgHom_id]
   148	  right_inv F := by
   149	    rw [← mapAlgHom_comp, show e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k A' from
   150	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.apply_symm_apply a, mapAlgHom_id]
   151	
   152	/-- The transport along an isomorphism is `mapAlgHom` of its underlying map. -/
   153	@[simp]
   154	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') (F : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   155	    congr e F = mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom F :=
   156	  rfl
   157	
   158	/-- The inverse transport along an isomorphism is `mapAlgHom` of the inverse map. -/
   159	@[simp]
   160	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') (F : DivFamZar C A' π n) :
   161	    (congr e).symm F = mapAlgHom e.symm.toAlgHom F :=
   162	  rfl

   180	/-- **The locally certified divisor functor at an arbitrary test object**
   181	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6 on the Addendum-2 carrier; the `divFam` vehicle):
   182	compatible families of locally certified divisor classes over the affine opens of
   183	`T.left` — the value at a smaller affine open is the base change of the value at a
   184	larger one along the section-restriction algebra map.  On affine tests this is
   185	`DivFamZar` itself (`divFamZarAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its canonical
   186	Zariski-continuous extension. -/

   188	  {s : Π U : T.left.affineOpens, DivFamZar C Γ(T.left, U.1) π n //
   189	    ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),

   196	/-- The compatibility of a section of `divFamZar` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/

   198	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
   199	  s.2 U V h

   234	direction of the affine comparison. -/

    11	/-!
    12	# The widened divisor-functor map (R2, human decision I-0492)
    13	
    14	`DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` along an arbitrary test change `R → R'`, with the functor laws, the Abel
    15	hook, and the Zariski separation keystone.  This is what makes the widened value a functor
    16	VALUE rather than a bare type: before this file nothing could base-change a widened class.
    17	
    18	## Where the widening does and does not show
    19	
    20	Almost nowhere.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` widens where the pieces live on the CURVE and changes
    21	nothing about the Zariski cover of the BASE, so the base-side machinery of
    22	`DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg.lean` — the `Localization.Away` towers, `IsLocalization.map`,
    23	`span_range_algebraMap_eq_top` — applies verbatim; the cover datum only appears inside the
    24	opaque `mapAlg` of the local certified family.  Likewise
    25	`Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback`, `divEq_pullback_id` and `divEq_pullback_pullback` are
    26	stated for ARBITRARY scheme morphisms and know nothing about covers, so the functor laws are
    27	the same three lines as in the chart-typed case.
    28	
    29	## The one honest cost of the widening: overlap affineness
    30	
    31	`AffCoverData` demands affineness of the pieces only (that is the R2 shape), so the certificate
    32	transport takes an explicit `hinf` — the overlaps are affine.  A `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff`
    33	therefore cannot be base-changed without it, and rather than weaken the structure this file
    34	carries `hinf` as a hypothesis on `mapAlg` at the family level.  It is not a hidden
    35	assumption: it is visible in every signature below, as I-0492 clause 4 requires.  For a
    36	relative curve over a proper `C` it is discharged by separatedness (`IsAffineOpen.inf`).
    37	
    38	## Main declarations
    39	
    40	* `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg` — base change of a widened certified family.
    41	* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.pullback` — certificate transport along an arbitrary test change.
    42	* `DivFamZarAff.mapAlg`, with `mapAlg_mk`, `picClass_mapAlg`, `mapAlg_id`, `mapAlg_comp`.
    43	* `DivFamZarAff.eq_of_away_eq` — Zariski separation at the widened Zar level.
    44	-/

   186	              (⊤ : (overSpec k R).left.Opens) ≤ (⊤ : (overSpec k R).left.Opens))
   187	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k R).left, ⊤) from Over.resAlgHom_rfl _ le_top,
   188	          AlgHom.id_comp,
   189	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom.comp
   190	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom
   191	            = AlgHom.id k R from
   192	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).apply_symm_apply a]
   193	    _ = x := DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_id x
   194	
   195	/-- **The widened affine comparison equivalence**: on an affine test `overSpec k R`, the
   196	widened affine-opens limit collapses by evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the
   197	affine-opens poset to the widened value `DivFamZarAff C R n` of the test algebra.
   198	
   199	This is what makes the vehicle a genuine extension rather than a new object: the widened
   200	certificate lane's endpoint lands in the right-hand side, so this equivalence is the step that
   201	carries it into the vehicle.
   202	
   203	**Exactly how far that reaches, stated so nobody over-reads it.**  It carries the endpoint into
   204	a vehicle *section over an affine test*, and no further.  Getting from there to a general test
   205	is `divFamZarAff.map` along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, which does **not** exist yet
   206	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 8 §8.3 item 2); its input is the widened form of the base-side
   207	Zariski gluing keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`.  So the honest reading of this
   208	file is: the widened value now has a vehicle and collapses correctly on affine tests; the
   209	Zariski-continuous *extension* to all tests is still owed. -/
   210	def divFamZarAffAffineEquiv :
   211	    divFamZarAff C n (overSpec k R) ≃ DivFamZarAff C R n where
   212	  toFun := divFamZarAffToAff C n R
   213	  invFun := divFamZarAffOfAff C n R
   214	  left_inv := divFamZarAffOfAff_divFamZarAffToAff C n R
   215	  right_inv := divFamZarAffToAff_divFamZarAffOfAff C n R
   216	
   217	/-- The widened affine comparison evaluates at the top affine open and transports along
   218	`Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv`. -/
   219	@[simp]
   220	lemma divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_apply (s : divFamZarAff C n (overSpec k R)) :
   221	    divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n R s
   222	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom
   223	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine R)) :=
   224	  rfl
   225	
   226	/-- The inverse widened affine comparison restricts the transported class from the top affine
   227	open. -/
   228	@[simp]
   229	lemma divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_symm_apply_val (x : DivFamZarAff C R n)
   230	    (U : (overSpec k R).left.affineOpens) :
   231	    ((divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n R).symm x).1 U
   232	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
   233	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top).comp
   234	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
   235	  rfl
   236	
   237	end Affine
   238	
   239	/-! ## The comparison from the chart-typed vehicle
   240	
   241	`DivFamZar.toAff` (`…AffCompare.lean`) sends a chart-typed class to a widened one at a single
   242	affine test, and `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` (`…AffFace.lean`) makes that compatible with
   243	restriction on the explicit face.  Together they lift the comparison to the *vehicles*, which is
   244	what a consumer holding a section over a general test needs.
   245	
   246	The direction is old → new and only old → new.  That is not a limitation of the construction: it
   247	is the content of R2.  A widened certificate cover is an arbitrary family of affine opens, and by
   248	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every
   249	genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can confine, so no map back can exist. -/

      "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently. All seven verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk:\n\n D DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean   (hdegAff DISCHARGED -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff.lean        (the WIDENED Sigma-chart -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean            (the V=bot refutation -- p4, this round)\n D Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean           (p2's locus work, this round)\n D roadmap items .../c9-chartlocus.chart-u-aff.yaml  (p3's new row)\n D roadmap comments AJCR.w4-rep/C-0011.md            (my re-ranking)\n D roadmap comments .../abel-widened/C-0003.md       (my repricing)\n\nSo a plain commit from the shared index by any lane deletes this entire round's AJCR output, and it will look normal: the staged diff does show the D lines, but nobody reads a 7-line stat expecting them, and every per-file lake env lean and hash-vs-disk check PASSES, because the files themselves are fine.     10	# Certified base change on the widened cover (R2, human decision I-0492)
    11	
    12	The seven certificate clauses of `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` transport along an arbitrary test
    13	change `R → R'`.  This is the last structural piece the widened value needed: without it
    14	`DivFamZarAff` is a type with no functoriality, and nothing downstream can base-change a
    15	widened class.
    16	
    17	## Two definitional identities do most of the work
    18	
    19	Both were probed and hold on the nose, which is why this file is short:
    20	
    21	* the base-changed overlap **is** the preimage of the overlap
    22	  (`(D.baseChange R').pieces i ⊓ (D.baseChange R').pieces j = relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ (pieces i ⊓
    23	  pieces j)` by `rfl`, since `⁻¹ᵁ` commutes with `⊓` definitionally on `Opens`);
    24	* the pulled colength **is** the quotient `relQuotBaseChangeAff` lands in.
    25	
    26	So the widened colength and overlap transports are the SAME declaration
    27	(`AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`) at two different opens, where the chart-typed layer
    28	needed `pieceQuotBaseChange` and a separately-constructed `ovlQuotBaseChange` conjugated
    29	through the overlap generator.
    30	
    31	## What is reused verbatim
    32	
    33	Clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) ride the abstract `FlatCokernel` keystones
    34	(`LinearMap.ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker`, `LinearMap.tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker`,
    35	`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`) and the two square-transport lemmas
    36	(`LinearEquiv.map_ker_of_comp_eq`, `LinearEquiv.range_eq_map_range_of_comp_eq`).  All are
    37	stated for bare modules and know nothing about covers, so the widening does not touch them.
    38	
    39	## Main declarations
    40	
    41	* `AffAdaptation.colengthBaseChange`, `ovlColengthBaseChange` — the (c1) and overlap
    42	  transports, both `AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`.
    43	* `AffAdaptation.chartProdBaseChange`, `ovlProdBaseChange` — the product transports.
    44	* `AffAdaptation.delta_baseChange_comm` — `δ`-naturality, a `funext` over the pair index.
    45	* `AffAdaptation.gluedBaseChange` and the (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transports.
    46	* `AffAdaptation.isCertified_pullback` — **the certificate base-changes**, all seven clauses.
    47	-/

     9	# STEP 1 OF THE CLASSIFIER, WIDENED: a widened class has certified away representatives
    10	
    11	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.cert-assemble`; the *classifier* direction.
    12	
    13	`…AffSeedGate.lean` / `…AffSeedSection.lean` gave the widened carrier a producer from geometry, so
    14	`divFunctorAff` now receives values.  The other half of `DivRepGlobalData` is the **classifier**
    15	`divRepClassifyZar` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:244`), and its route begins with
    16	
    17	  `DivFamZar.exists_certified_away_rep`  (`DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:79`)
    18	
    19	— step 1 of the ddr9 worksheet: a locally certified class restricts, on a finite span-`⊤` family
    20	of basic opens of the base, to *classes of certified families* over the away localizations.
    21	
    22	This file is that theorem at `DivFamZarAff`.
    23	
    24	## Why this port is legitimate, and why it is the RIGHT next brick
    25	
    26	`…AffFraming.lean` already scoped what a widened classifier needs, and correctly identified that
    27	`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` — step 1 **plus** the ε-framing — does not port wholesale,
    28	because its proof runs through the two-chart `PairChartRing` window.  That remains true, and this
    29	file does not claim otherwise.
    30	
    31	What this file observes is that step 1 **by itself** contains no chart content whatsoever.  Read
    32	the chart-typed proof: it takes a `Quotient` representative, reads the `IsLocallyCertified`
    33	existential the subtype carries, and repackages the recorded `DivEq` as a `mk`-equality.  Every
    34	step is about the quotient and the base-side away family; `π` appears only in the *type* of the
    35	carrier, never in an argument.  So the widened statement is provable by the same four moves at
    36	`DivFamZarAff`, and the two places the spellings differ are exactly the two ADDENDUM 9 §9.2 warns

    38	family's own local certifiability is `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.isLocallyCertifiedAff` rather than

    69	variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] {n : ℕ}
    70	
    71	/-- **Step 1 of the classifier, at the widened carrier.**  A widened locally certified class over
    72	`S` restricts, on a finite span-`⊤` family of basic opens, to the classes of *widened* certified
    73	divisor families over the canonical away localizations.
    74	
    75	The chart-typed twin is `DivFamZar.exists_certified_away_rep` (`DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:79`), and
    76	the proof is the same four moves — take a quotient representative, read the pin's existential,
    77	recover the recorded `DivEq`, repackage as a `mk`-equality.  No step mentions a chart, a partition,
    78	or `π`: step 1 is entirely about the quotient and the Zariski cover of the BASE, which R2 did not
    79	touch.

    81	`[IsProper C.hom]` is carried because the widened `mapAlg` needs it (ADDENDUM 6 item 3: an
    82	arbitrary affine open's overlaps are not affine by fiat), and it is a hypothesis the DD-R lane has
    83	everywhere. -/
    84	theorem DivFamZarAff.exists_certified_away_rep (F₀ : DivFamZarAff C S n) :
    85	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤ ∧
    86	      ∀ l : Fin m, ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (h l)) n,
    87	        G.toZarAff = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg (Localization.Away (h l)) n F₀ := by
    88	  obtain ⟨dp, hdp⟩ := Quotient.exists_rep F₀
    89	  obtain ⟨m, h, hspan, hG⟩ := dp.2
    90	  refine ⟨m, h, hspan, fun l => ?_⟩
    91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C S (Localization.Away (h l))) :=
    92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C S (Localization.Away (h l)) (h l)
    93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG l
    94	  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
    95	  rw [← hdp]
    96	  exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr hGdiv
    97	
    98	/-- Step 1 read at an explicit system and pin, for a caller who has just produced one (e.g. from
    99	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_swallowing_affineOpen`) and has not packaged the
   100	class yet. -/
   101	theorem DivFamZarAff.exists_certified_away_rep_of_mk
   102	    {d : (relCurve C S).LocalEquations} (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
   103	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤ ∧
   104	      ∀ l : Fin m, ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (h l)) n,
   105	        G.toZarAff = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg (Localization.Away (h l)) n
   106	          (DivFamZarAff.mk d hd) :=
   107	  DivFamZarAff.exists_certified_away_rep _

    10	# Rank-one fibre quotients
    11	
    12	If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
    13	fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.
    14	
    15	The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
    16	`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
    17	quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
    18	neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
    19	-/

    31	/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
    32	of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
    33	no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
    34	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    35	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    36	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    37	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    38	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    39	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    40	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    41	  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    42	    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
    43	  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    44	    intro v
    45	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    46	    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
    47	      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    48	    simp
    49	  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    50	    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    51	    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    52	    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    53	    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
    54	  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton

    82	  exact hfs

    84	/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
    85	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    86	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    87	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    88	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    89	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    90	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    91	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    92	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    93	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
    94	  apply Subtype.ext
    95	  exact hfs
    96	
    97	/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
    98	that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.
    99	
   100	For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
   101	vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
   102	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   103	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   104	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   105	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   106	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
   107	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   108	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   109	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   110	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   111	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
   112	  simpa using hfs
   113	
   114	/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
   115	This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
   116	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
   117	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   118	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   119	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   120	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
   121	      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   122	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   123	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   124	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
   125	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
   126	  simpa using hfs
   127	
   128	/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
   129	a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
   130	theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   131	    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   132	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
   133	    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
   134	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
   135	    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
   136	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
   137	    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
   138	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
   139	  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   140	  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s
   141	
   142	end RankOneFibre

   144	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength
    11	
    12	This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
    13	to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
    14	span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
    15	colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	open scoped TensorProduct
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    29	
    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    31	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    32	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    33	
    34	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    35	
    36	/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
    37	pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
    38	`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
    39	`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
    40	zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
    41	it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
    42	theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    43	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    44	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    45	    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    46	    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
    47	        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    48	        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
    49	          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
    50	            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    51	            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
    52	              by
    53	                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
    54	              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    55	    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
    56	      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    57	  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
    58	  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
    59	  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
    60	  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
    61	  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    62	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
    63	  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    64	    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    65	    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
    66	  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    67	    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
    68	      intro v
    69	      exact hspan v) hfs
    70	  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
    71	  exact hzero
    72	
    73	end ThetaGeneratorSeed
    74	
    75	end AlgebraicGeometry
